concept: Atlas Credits Prepaid Subscriptions and Overage
summary: Atlas bills against five subscription types: Elastic (a monthly invoice for usage, no commitment), Prepaid (credits bought up front for a chosen term), Flex Commitment (unused credits are charged in the last month of the term), Monthly Commitment (the greater of usage or the prorated monthly commitment, with unused credits covering later overages) and Marketplace. Available credits are drawn down in the order shown in the Available Credits table; when a Monthly Commitment organization runs out of credits it transitions to Elastic Billing and usage beyond the credits is billed, and when a subscription expires Atlas charges remaining usage to the payment method on file and reverts paid support plans to Basic. This pack draws on 4 source pages across 2 host labels and covers definitions, structure, mechanism, how-to, examples, measures, problems and history; the only independent figures (a 3-year default commit with a 15 to 30 percent annual ramp) come from a buyer-side advisory firm and are marked unverified.

facts.text: Atlas subscription types are Elastic (monthly invoice for usage, no commitment), Prepaid (credits bought up front for a chosen term), Flex Commitment, Monthly Commitment and Marketplace. Purchase of commitments goes through MongoDB Sales; activation needs Organization Owner or Organization Billing Admin.

Flex Commitment: unused credits are charged in the last month of the term. Monthly Commitment: each month bills the greater of usage or the prorated monthly commitment, and unused credits carry forward to cover later overages in the term.
You commit to paying for several credits for a term, such as annual, and receive a monthly invoice for your usage. Unused credits are charged in the last month of the subscription's term.

You commit to paying for several credits for a term, such as annual, and receive a monthly invoice for the greater of your usage or your prorated monthly commitment. You can apply unused credits at a later date during the term to cover overages.
You prepay for credits, usable for a term you define upon subscribing, such as annual.

A MongoDB subscription offers flexible payment terms and advanced support options. Subscriptions allow for billing in different currencies, billing in arrears, billing monthly or for annual invoicing with ACH payments or wire transfers. Subscriptions provide order forms [1] and an Enterprise Customer Service Agreement (CSA).
Elastic Billing subscriptions, represented as infinite available credit. An active Elastic Billing subscription means you're charged for Atlas usage as you go.
You receive a monthly invoice for your usage.
You receive invoices for your Atlas usage through the marketplace from which you subscribed.
Payment methods, which may include Atlas credits from a prepaid subscription or promotional subscription, a monthly commitment subscription, a marketplace subscription, a credit card, or PayPal.

Invoices list credits as a payment method; CSV exports contain a row whose Description contains 'Credit' with a negative Amount (filter it out to compute the subtotal, or use it to see when credits ran out). Invoice status PREPAID means the prepaid subscription covered the invoice with credits.
Lists payment methods, which may include Atlas credits from a prepaid or promotional subscription, a monthly commitment subscription, a marketplace subscription, PayPal, or a credit card.
If your subscription includes a commitment for a term, such as annual, you can you can view your month's spending against your commitment on your organization's Available Credits table.
Your active available credits. Active credit items display a progress bar to show your usage to date of that total pool of credits.
Upcoming available credits that you have not yet started to spend, displayed in gray.
VIEW DETAILS: view your subscription's monthly commitment details.
An Elastic Billing Enabled indicator if your organization has Elastic Billing enabled.

On Google Cloud Monthly Commitment the monthly minimum is total commitment divided by months; once cumulative usage exceeds the total commitment, the account moves to elastic billing and pays the minimum plus elastic usage.

If a Monthly Commitment org runs out of credits it automatically transitions to Elastic Billing, and usage beyond credits is billed. The transition produces two tax invoices for the same billing period. The Elastic Billing indicator shows only that it is enabled, not that it is active.

If you use all your monthly commitment subscription credits before your subscription expires and your subscription has Elastic Billing enabled, Atlas bills you for usage beyond your subscription credits. When your Monthly Commitment Subscription transitions to Elastic Billing:

Available credits are drawn down from the top item to the bottom in the order shown in the Available Credits table; upcoming credits appear grey and are not yet spent. Expired credits appear in the History table.

The pop-up informational card opens that shows the details of your monthly commitment for your subscription. This card compares your subscription commitment to your usage during the invoice period. You are charged the greater of your monthly commit or your usage. Unused credits are applied to cover overages during the term of your subscription.

After your cumulative subscription usage exceeds your total commitment value, Atlas transitions your account to elastic billing. With elastic billing, Atlas bills you the full value of your usage each month for the remainder of your commitment. Your Google Cloud invoice reflects your elastic billing charges in addition to your monthly minimum commitment.

At the end of the month, if your usage is lower than your prorated monthly commitment, you are charged for the prorated commitment. Unused credits can be applied at a later date during the term to cover overages.
If Elastic Billing is enabled, an indicator displays at the top of the Available Credits table.

If you have a subscription with an amount due, your invoice's Payment Details section displays the PAY NOW action in the Actions column for the subscription payment method. This allows you to pay your tax invoices for your monthly commitment or elastic subscription directly from the YayPay website.

The Elastic Billing indicator does not necessarily mean your Elastic Billing subscription is active, only that it is enabled. If you run out of credits, your organization automatically transitions to Elastic Billing.
Your prepaid subscription has covered the invoice with credits.

With a Google Cloud Monthly Commitment subscription, you have a minimum monthly commitment you must pay Google each month. Your minimum monthly amount due is your total commitment value divided by the number of months in your commitment. Whether you use less or more than your monthly commitment, you are billed at least this amount.

A cloud usage summary detailing your MongoDB Cloud usage, viewable in Atlas on your organization's Billing page. The format is similar to cloud invoices for customers without a subscription, but usage summary values are in credits not USD.
Your cloud invoice displays an Atlas Elastic Invoice and your final Atlas Monthly Commit payment in the Payment Details
Available credits are drawn from the top item to the bottom in the order they appear on the table.
If you purchase a MongoDB subscription from a marketplace, you don't receive a tax invoice. Instead, you receive an invoice with an amount due through that marketplace.

Your cloud usage summary represents MongoDB Cloud usage in credits and doesn't account for currency conversions or other adjustments. The tax invoice emailed to your billing contact provides the amount to pay.
If you have an active Elastic Billing subscription, you are charged for your usage as you go.

If you are a YayPay customer, you can pay your monthly commitment or elastic invoices directly from the Payment Details section of your invoice page. To learn more, see View and Pay Your Current Invoice.

Billed Usage: the amount you are being billed for. Billed Usage amount can differ from the usage amount in a number of cases, such as when a month's usage is below the monthly minimum on your Atlas subscription, or a month's billed usage encompasses usage for multiple months.
The Used column displays your elastic usage to date.
In each one of your invoices, the Summary By Project and Summary By Service tables list your usage in terms of Atlas credits.
This information helps you calculate when you ran out of credits. When summing the Amount column, you can filter out this row to calculate your invoice subtotal.
Atlas creates the following event: Active Invoicing Period initiated. MongoDB will invoice your organization based on your monthly usage.

With this new listing and integration, you can pay via AWS with no upfront commitments. Simply subscribe via AWS Marketplace and start using Atlas. You can get started for free with Atlas’s free-forever tier, then scale as needed. You’ll be charged in AWS only for the resources you use in Atlas, with no payment minimum. Deploy, scale, and tear down resources in Atlas as needed; you’ll pay just for the hours that you’re using them.
To purchase a subscription, you can contact MongoDB Sales or purchase one through a marketplace.
When you purchase a subscription from MongoDB Sales, MongoDB sends you an email containing an activation code. To apply this subscription to your Atlas organization:
To view your expired credits, see the History table located below the Available Credits table.
When you purchase a subscription, you are asked to provide a billing contact email address. Your billing contact receives invoices.
You must be an Organization Owner or Organization Billing Admin to activate a subscription.
Locate the Atlas monthly commitment in the Payment method column.
Locate the Total column for the Atlas monthly commitment row.
Click the Apply Code button.
Enter your Activation Code.
If you lose your activation code, request support.

For a $12,000 total annual commitment, after you accrue $12,000 of usage, Google Cloud bills the monthly commitment of $1,000 plus any additional usage as reported by Atlas. If your usage for a given month after you exhaust your total annual commitment is $4,000, Google Cloud charges $5,000 for that month ($1,000 monthly minimum + $4,000 elastic billing).
A buyer-side advisory firm (Redress Compliance, unsourced estimates, sells negotiation services) claims a default 3-year Atlas Credits commit with 15-30% annual ramp; treat as unverified.
15 to 30 percent default annual Atlas Credits ramp across the contracted three year term
3 year default 2026 MongoDB Atlas Credits commit term
20 to 45 percent typical 2026 MongoDB Atlas opening renewal commercial uplift

When a subscription expires, Atlas charges remaining usage to the payment method on file, reverts paid support plans to Basic, risks suspension if the payment method declines, and bills unpaid charges on the next subscription activation. Deployments must be terminated to stop charges.
If a subscription activation code is not added within the first 30 days of use, MongoDB charges the account's credit card, and card charges are non-refundable.
Atlas reverts your organization to the free Basic support plan from any paid plan that you purchased with your subscription.
Once you activate your next subscription, Atlas bills you for any unpaid charges. If your subscription becomes delayed, contact your MongoDB Sales representative.
If you do not add your subscription activation code within the first 30 days of use, MongoDB charges the credit card associated with the account. Credit card charges are non-refundable.

If you have no payment method added to your organization, Atlas prompts you to set a payment method when you make billing changes through the Atlas UI or Admin API. If your payment method declines, your account is at risk of suspension.
To stop incurring any future charges, you must terminate your deployments.

Direct Atlas pay as you go accepts credit card, PayPal and invoice with no minimum; the AWS Marketplace pay-as-you-go listing removed the earlier upfront-commitment requirement (page updated 2025-09-23).

Previously, customers who wanted to pay via AWS Marketplace had to commit to a certain level of usage upfront. Pay as you go is available directly in Atlas via credit card, PayPal, and invoice — but not in AWS Marketplace, until today.
